title: Understanding Cloud & Branch Connector Software Updates

blocks.text: When you deploy Cloud & Branch Connectors, they automatically update to the latest software versions based on the schedule. Cloud & Branch Connectors check for new software versions every week, and if one is available, they upgrade automatically. By default, the upgrade window starts every Sunday at midnight (local time of the deployed Cloud or Branch Connector). When a new version is available, connectors in a Cloud Connector group or Branch Connector group are updated in a sequence, one at a time, so the group keeps forwarding traffic. While updating, the connector restarts and becomes temporarily unavailable, and the traffic is handled by other connectors in the group.
After deployment, you can view the release channel and upgrade status of virtual machines (VMs) on the Upgrade Manager page.

blocks.heading: Package Updates vs. Full Image Refresh or Redeployment

blocks.text: The weekly upgrade delivers most new software as package or repo updates. However, kernel, OS-level, or platform changes are not a part of the package repo and require a full image refresh by redeploying the connector from the latest image. The method of the image refresh depends on how the connector is deployed:

blocks.item: Autoscaling group (AWS) / Scale sets (Azure) / Managed Instance Group (MIG) autoscaling (GCP)

This is an easy and effectively automatic method. Instances are launched from a template or image, and you can choose the latest image by recycling instances. For example, an instance refresh in AWS or rolling the scale set includes the latest image with no manual rebuild. By default, the deployment templates pull the latest Cloud Connector image from the marketplace.

Images are refreshed only when deployed, and there is no automatic recycling. Zscaler recommends that you redeploy individually deployed Cloud Connectors at least once a year with the latest image to align with operating system (OS) or platform changes.

blocks.heading: About Cloud & Branch Connector OS Management

blocks.text: Zscaler delivers the Cloud & Branch Connector as a managed appliance image and is responsible for maintaining and upgrading both the connector software and the underlying OS. You are not responsible for patching the connector OS. However, deployments on your own cloud or hypervisor infrastructure for the host (e.g., networking and access to upgrade endpoints) is your organization's responsibility.
Service level agreement commitments for critical OS security patches are governed by Zscaler's agreement. To learn more, see Zscaler SLA & Support.
